title: introduce-region-aware-kms-quotas-and-audit-fence-middleware
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customers requested stronger guardrails for large cross-region KMS operations and tighter observability for KMS-related costs. We observed two incidents where high-volume KMS wrap/unwrap storms originating from a mis-deployed operator caused downstream quotas to be exceeded in a single region and produced noisy audit logs. This PR introduces a region-aware KMS usage quota layer + an "audit fence" middleware that canonicalizes and samples KMS call proofs to make audits actionable without overwhelming ingestion.

What this PR does: Adds a light-weight quota controller that tracks KMS op counts and byte-usage per (tenant, region, key-type) window and enforces soft and hard limits with graded responses (log-only -> rate-limit -> reject). Integrates quota decisions into RBAC v2 predicates so cross-region KMS requests without explicit residency consent are denied at the authz layer. Implements an audit-fence middleware that: 1) canonicalizes KMS provenance headers into a compact proof token, 2) samples high-volume events and emits a summary envelope to the audit pipeline, and 3) attaches quota stamp metadata so downstream billing/ops can correlate spikes with region scope.

Key design points: - Region-first accounting: quotas are keyed by claimed region then reconciled against actual KMS provider location (best-effort) to catch mismatches. - Tiered enforcement: default soft limits for self-serve tenants; stricter limits for free accounts; reserved capacity tenants get higher thresholds. Limits and policies are configurable through policy templates in pkg/kms/quota/templates. - RBAC integration: new predicate rbac/conditions/region_kms_allowed.go consults tenant metadata (region_pin, operator_consent) and quota decisions during policy evaluation. - Audit scaling: the fence converts verbose wrap/unwrap events into digest-sized proof tokens (HMAC of minimal provenance fields) and publishes sampled envelopes to audit-stream to reduce ingestion cost while preserving reconstructability for investigations.

Files changed (high level): listed below — small code changes to policy compiler and test harness, a new quota controller, middleware, tests, and docs.

Migration notes: - Config: operators must populate region_pin for tenants that require residency guarantees. New default quotas are included in 00-defaults.yaml; tenant admins can override per-tenant. - Runtime: the middleware is opt-in via feature flag KMS_REGION_QUOTA in the deployment config; we enable it in staging for two weeks before global rollout. - Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is off the middleware is no-op and RBAC predicate returns neutral (no deny).

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover quota window math, RBAC predicate decision matrix, and HMAC proof token generation. - Integration tests run against a simulated KMS backend with region labels to ensure enforcement path and sampling are correct. - Load test (perf-canary) validated that fence sampling reduces audit ingestion by ~82% under synthetic wrap/unwrap storm.

Rollback plan: Feature flag toggle to disable middleware; quota controller has a safe default to fall back to log-only. Database migrations are backwards compatible (new tables for quota state with TTL).

Checklist: - [x] Quota controller implementation and core tests - [x] RBAC predicate + unit tests - [x] Audit-fence middleware + integration tests - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan - [x] Security review and threat model added to docs

Related: ENG-2191 (quota framework), SEC-402 (audit scaling), also touches on operator onboarding docs and billing telemetry.

ci_checks: codecov: marginal drop in unrelated files (-0.1%)
release_notes: - Introduced region-aware KMS usage quotas with tiered enforcement and per-tenant overrides. - Added audit-fence middleware to canonicalize KMS provenance and reduce audit ingestion while preserving investigatory proofs. - RBAC v2 predicate prevents cross-region KMS calls for tenants without residency consent. Feature gated behind KMS_REGION_QUOTA flag; enable in staging first.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in staging (deploy/staging/kms-fence-enabled.yaml). Watch metrics kms_quota_rejections, kms_quota_soft_hits, audit_fence_sample_rate. Billing and ops should subscribe to kms_quota_alerts channel during rollout.
security_review: Threat model and mitigations added to docs/security/kms-region-quotas.md. Key handling uses KMS-wrapped rotation; proof tokens are HMAC over minimal fields and do not contain PII. Manual review by security approved SEC-402.
user_impact: Most tenants will see no change at default thresholds. Self-serve tenants may observe soft-limit logging then progressive throttling if they exceed regional KMS quotas. Reserved capacity customers are unaffected by default limits but can opt-in to additional protection.
